title: PersonaCard
description: Declarative SME-persona card (EPIC-00, issue #4; issue #11): the packaged, tenant-scoped definition of a subject-matter-expert persona (name, expertise, owned lanes, default model tier, guardrails) that maps onto an AgentProfile (issue #9). A persona belongs to a tenant or to the platform default ('tenant: platform'); tenants extend the library by adding their own card files under registry/personas/cards/ (one file per persona — the loader discovers all cards by scanning the directory, so adding a file adds a persona with no code change). The vocabulary enums below are a snapshot of the CLOSED platform vocabulary owned by registry/profiles/catalog.yaml (issue #9); registry/personas/registry.py additionally enforces fail-closed membership against the LIVE catalog so the two can never silently drift. Lifecycle state (draft/published/retired) is NOT a card field: publish/retire are recorded in the append-only versions/manifest.yaml ledger (registry.py), keeping published card content immutable via sha256.

id.description: Stable persona id (lowercase, dash-separated, e.g. security-sme, orchestrator). Must equal the card filename stem (<id>.yaml). A persona maps to an AgentProfile whose id is this value.

version.description: SemVer version of THIS persona card (X.Y.Z). A published (tenant, persona, version) is immutable: the registry records the card's sha256 in versions/manifest.yaml and refuses to resolve a published card whose content no longer matches. Improving a published persona means authoring a new card version and publishing it.

tenant.description: The tenant that owns this persona. 'platform' is reserved for platform-default personas shared with every tenant. Any other value is a tenant id: that tenant may extend the library with its own cards (and may shadow a platform-default persona of the same id). A persona is resolved tenant-first with a documented platform fallback — never across other tenants.

name.description: Display name of the persona (e.g. 'Security SME').

summary.description: One-line summary of what this persona is for and when to dispatch it.

expertise.description: Areas of expertise this persona brings (stack, disciplines, standards). Used by review assignment for domain scoring.

ownedLanes.description: The lanes / issue families this persona owns (e.g. security, guardrails). SME-card convention (shared-frontend SME-PROFILES). Free-form lane ids are open across tenants.

posture.description: Operational class, enforcing separation of duties: 'executor' performs primary work (write/run/ship); 'reviewer' independently reviews an executor's PR/verdict; 'auditor' adversarially audits claims/evidence. An auditor persona is never the executing persona of the task it audits (registry/personas/mapping.py guard_dispatch rejects it).

defaultModelTier.description: Default dispatch tier on the flash/pro ladder (LOW/MED -> flash, HIGH/MAX -> pro). Closed platform vocabulary (issue #9 catalog tiers). Security/architecture personas carry HIGH/MAX floors; reviewers with verification duty default LOW/MED.

guardrailPolicyRef.description: Single guardrail policy bound to this persona (atomic id or bundle id from the issue #9 guardrail-policy catalog). Executor workers bind worker-bundle; reviewer/auditor personas bind reviewer-bundle.

systemPromptRef.description: Pinned reference to the persona's primary system-prompt module in the prompt library (issue #13), shape <module>/<name>@v<n> (e.g. security-sme/primary@v1). Matches the AgentProfile systemPromptRef convention (issue #9 seeds use <role>/primary@v1). Module publication is owned by the prompt-library lane; the mapping pins the reference shape.

toolAllowlist.description: Closed allowlist of platform tool ids this persona may invoke (issue #9 catalog). Unknown tool => rejected (fail closed). Reviewer/auditor personas use a verify-only tool set.

capabilitySet.description: Closed capability set this persona may exercise (issue #9 catalog). Unknown capability => rejected (fail closed). A capability whose declared requirements (integrations/paperclip/reporting/capability.py) name a tool the persona's toolAllowlist does not grant is refused by name — declared and usable must not diverge (issue #447).

constraintSet.description: Boundary constraints (deny/require rules) this persona operates under (issue #9 catalog). Unknown constraint => rejected (fail closed).

memoryScope.description: Memory scopes this persona may read/write (issue #9 catalog memory scopes). At least one scope required.

provenance.description: Record of the read-only source(s) this persona card was derived from, as '<repo> <path>' strings (GR-10 provenance doctrine, docs/CANNIBALIZATION.md).

description.description: Longer narrative of the persona's role, discriminating focus and doctrine (optional).

guardrails.description: Human-readable non-negotiables this persona operates under (the SME card 'Guardrails' section; optional — machine enforcement rides on guardrailPolicyRef + constraintSet).

role.description: Canonical CMR agent role this persona fills (CMR onboarding/agent-profiles/role.schema.json). Optional: a platform persona (coder, orchestrator, ...) need not map to a CMR role, but an SME persona derived from a CMR role MUST name it, and the id must exist in the canonical CMR role vocabulary (the registry/parity gate enforces the mirror, issue #145).

model.description: Concrete worker model for the default tier (flash or pro). Separates the MODEL axis from the tier axis (leaderboard fleet-roster ROLE/TIER/MODEL/TRANSPORT/EFFORT separation). Optional.

transport.description: How the model is carried: a provider API (deepseek/api) or the running CLI session (session). Separates the TRANSPORT axis (leaderboard lib/fleet-roster.sh role_transport). Optional.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this persona's dispatches (low/medium/high; leaderboard lib/fleet-roster.sh role_effort). Separates the EFFORT axis. Optional.

capabilityTier.description: Capability tier (deep/balanced/fast; leaderboard fleet-roster three-tier routing), distinct from the semantic model tier. Optional.

fallbackChain.description: Ordered fallback chain of canonical role ids to dispatch when this persona cannot serve the task (capital-underwriting config/leaderboard/capability-registry.json 'fallback' pattern). Every id must be a canonical CMR role. Optional.

canonicalLanes.description: Canonical CMR lane ids this persona owns (CMR role schema ownedLanes). Optional cross-walk to the CMR lane taxonomy; distinct from the free-form ownedLanes field above.

weekly_spend_ceiling.description: First-class per-persona FinOps ceiling: the maximum the platform may spend on this persona in a rolling week, in USD. Optional; when absent the persona is governed by the platform default budget guardrail. When present it must be a non-negative number (a negative ceiling is refused by the schema and by registry/personas/registry.py).

reportsTo.description: Org-chart reporting line (issue #632): the platform persona id this persona reports to, or the reserved principal 'board' for the org chart's single root. Optional and backwards-compatible — a persona without a reporting line is simply not part of the declared org chart. The id must be a resolvable platform persona (or 'board'), and the edge must appear in registry/personas/org-chart.yaml: registry.validate_org_chart() refuses an unresolvable edge.

monthlyBudgetCapUsd.description: First-class per-persona MONTHLY FinOps cap in USD (issue #632 C-suite workbook row). Optional and backwards-compatible. Distinct from the rolling-week weekly_spend_ceiling: this is the monthly ceiling the org chart declares per role (e.g. CEO $300.00, CFO $50.00). When present it must be a non-negative number; registry/personas/registry.py refuses a negative or non-numeric value fail-closed.

heartbeatSchedule.description: How often this persona's heartbeat is refreshed (issue #632 org chart). Optional and backwards-compatible. The closed vocabulary covers fixed cron cadences (hourly / every-30m / every-15m / daily) plus trigger-driven beats (event / webhook) — a heartbeat outside the platform cadences would be undispatchable, so the enum is closed. registry/personas/registry.py additionally refuses an unparseable value fail-closed.

roleId.description: Canonical CMR agent-role vocabulary (CMR onboarding/agent-profiles/role.schema.json properties.role.enum), backfilled per issue #145. The registry/parity gate fails if this set drifts from the canonical CMR role set in either direction.

modelTier.description: Dispatch tier on the flash/pro ladder (LOW/MED -> flash, HIGH/MAX -> pro). Closed platform vocabulary (issue #9 catalog tiers).

workerModel.description: Concrete worker model (CMR role schema model.model): flash = the volume tier, pro = the reasoning tier.

transport.description: Transport that carries the model (leaderboard lib/fleet-roster.sh role_transport): deepseek = the DeepSeek API path; api = the Anthropic API path; session = the running CLI session.

capabilityTier.description: Capability tier (leaderboard fleet-roster three-tier routing: deep/balanced/fast).

canonicalLane.description: Canonical CMR lane vocabulary (CMR role schema properties.ownedLanes.items.enum), backfilled per issue #145. The registry/parity gate fails on drift.

weeklySpendCeiling.description: Non-negative weekly spend ceiling in USD. Draft-07 treats booleans as a distinct type, so true/false fail here; registry/personas/registry.py additionally refuses a negative or non-numeric value fail-closed.

reportsTo.description: Org-chart reporting target (issue #632): a platform persona id from the C-suite org chart, plus the reserved principal 'board' (the principal OUTSIDE the agent org — the CEO's reporting line). Closed like every other platform vocabulary so a card can never name a reporting target that no persona can resolve; registry.validate_org_chart() additionally refuses an edge whose target is not a resolvable platform persona.

monthlyBudgetCapUsd.description: Non-negative MONTHLY budget cap in USD (issue #632 C-suite workbook row). Draft-07 treats booleans as a distinct type, so true/false fail here; registry/personas/registry.py additionally refuses a negative or non-numeric value fail-closed. Distinct from weekly_spend_ceiling (rolling week).

heartbeatSchedule.description: Closed heartbeat vocabulary (issue #632 org chart): hourly / every-30m / every-15m / daily are the fixed cron cadences; event / webhook are trigger-driven beats. A closed enum keeps every declared schedule dispatchable.
